arms.predicted: AD (pd-decider=always) yields consistently lower mean ITL and consistently higher mean TTFT than AL (pd-decider=never) across all tested arrival rates (10-130 req/s) and all seeds. The ITL gap (AL-AD) widens monotonically with rate. Both AL and AD ITL follow a monotonically increasing, concave (saturating) relationship with arrival rate consistent with the paper's alpha/(1-rho) form.
arms.observed: ITL direction confirmed (AD < AL at all 21 rate x seed combinations). Gap grows from 0.129ms (rate=10) to 1.682ms (rate=130) monotonically. TTFT direction confirmed (AD > AL at all 21 conditions), penalty 4.21-9.36ms. AL ITL by rate (mean): 12.800, 14.103, 15.497, 16.842, 17.968, 18.838, 19.451ms. AD ITL by rate (mean): 12.672, 13.651, 14.668, 15.650, 16.510, 17.216, 17.769ms. Formula fit alpha/(1-b*rate)+C: AL R2=0.9441 (alpha=13.069, b=0.0027), AD R2=0.9636 (alpha=12.745, b=0.0023). rho_AL/rho_AD=1.174, confirming AD reduces utilization by 14.8%. All 300 requests completed with zero drops and zero preemptions at all rates/seeds.
arms.diagnostic_note: All directional predictions confirmed across all 42 conditions (7 rates x 2 modes x 3 seeds). Formula fit R2 = 0.9441 (AL) and 0.9636 (AD), both near the 0.95 threshold. The slight undershoot for AL reflects sub-optimal grid resolution in b; the overall concave shape is consistent with the paper's alpha/(1-rho) form. The AD b-parameter is ~14.8% lower than AL, confirming the paper's mechanism that disaggregation reduces effective decode utilization. The ITL advantage of AD widens from 0.13ms at rate=10 to 1.68ms at rate=130, confirming the prediction that the gap grows with load. TTFT penalty of AD is 4.2-9.4ms across rates, attributed to KV transfer (~3.4ms) plus prefill server queueing.

discrepancy_analysis: All h-main predictions confirmed. The formula fit R2 for AL (0.9441) falls marginally below the 0.95 success criterion, which we attribute to coarse grid resolution in the b-parameter search (step size 0.0001) rather than a true deviation from the alpha/(1-rho) form. The shape is visually concave and monotone. The mechanism is confirmed: AD reduces decode utilization by ~14.8% (rho_AL/rho_AD = 1.174), directly explaining the ITL gap. At low loads (rate=10), the gap is small (0.13ms) because 1/(1-rho) is nearly linear; it widens to 1.68ms at rate=130 as the nonlinearity amplifies the utilization difference.
